nodes.summary: For $p \in [0, \infty]$, write $\ell^p_2$ for the space $\mathbb{R}^2$ regarded as the $\ell^p$ product of two copies of $\mathbb{R}$ (normed by the $\ell^p$ norm when $p \ge 1$). The vector $v_p \in \ell^p_2$ is $(1, -1)$, that is, $e_0 - e_1$, where $e_0 = (1, 0)$ and $e_1 = (0, 1)$ are the standard basis vectors.
nodes.title: The vector $(1, -1)$ in $\ell^p_2$

nodes.summary: For every $p \in [0, \infty]$, write $\ell^p_2$ for the space $\mathbb{R}^2$ regarded as the $\ell^p$ product of two copies of $\mathbb{R}$. The vectors $u_p = (1, 1)$ and $v_p = (1, -1)$ of $\ell^p_2$ satisfy $u_p + v_p = 2 e_0$, where $e_0 = (1, 0)$ is the first standard basis vector.
nodes.title: Sum of $(1, 1)$ and $(1, -1)$ in $\ell^p_2$

nodes.summary: For every $p \in [0, \infty]$, write $\ell^p_2$ for the space $\mathbb{R}^2$ regarded as the $\ell^p$ product of two copies of $\mathbb{R}$. The vectors $u_p = (1, 1)$ and $v_p = (1, -1)$ of $\ell^p_2$ satisfy $u_p - v_p = 2 e_1$, where $e_1 = (0, 1)$ is the second standard basis vector.
nodes.title: Difference of $(1, 1)$ and $(1, -1)$ in $\ell^p_2$

nodes.summary: For $p \in [0, \infty]$, write $\ell^p_2$ for the space $\mathbb{R}^2$ regarded as the $\ell^p$ product of two copies of $\mathbb{R}$ (normed by the $\ell^p$ norm when $p \ge 1$). The vector $u_p \in \ell^p_2$ is $(1, 1)$, that is, $e_0 + e_1$, where $e_0 = (1, 0)$ and $e_1 = (0, 1)$ are the standard basis vectors.
nodes.title: The vector $(1, 1)$ in $\ell^p_2$

nodes.summary: For every $p \in [1, \infty]$, let $\ell^p_2$ be $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^p$ norm, and let $u_p = (1, 1)$ and $v_p = (1, -1)$. Then $\|u_p + v_p\| = 2$.
nodes.title: Norm of $(1, 1) + (1, -1)$ in $\ell^p_2$

nodes.summary: For every real $p$ with $1 \le p < \infty$, the vector $(1, -1)$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ has $\ell^p$ norm $\|(1, -1)\|_p = 2^{1/p}$, where $\|(x, y)\|_p = (|x|^p + |y|^p)^{1/p}$.
nodes.title: The $\ell^p$ norm of $(1, -1)$ for finite $p$

nodes.summary: In $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^\infty$ norm $\|(x, y)\|_\infty = \max(|x|, |y|)$, the vector $(1, -1)$ has norm $\|(1, -1)\|_\infty = 1$.
nodes.title: The $\ell^\infty$ norm of $(1, -1)$

nodes.summary: For every real $p$ with $1 \le p < \infty$, the vector $(1, 1)$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ has $\ell^p$ norm $\|(1, 1)\|_p = 2^{1/p}$, where $\|(x, y)\|_p = (|x|^p + |y|^p)^{1/p}$.
nodes.title: The $\ell^p$ norm of $(1, 1)$ for finite $p$

nodes.summary: In $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^\infty$ norm $\|(x, y)\|_\infty = \max(|x|, |y|)$, the vector $(1, 1)$ has norm $\|(1, 1)\|_\infty = 1$.
nodes.title: The $\ell^\infty$ norm of $(1, 1)$

nodes.summary: For every real $p$ with $1 \le p < \infty$, the vector $(1, 1)$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ satisfies $\|(1, 1)\|_p^2 = 2^{2/p}$, where $\|(x, y)\|_p = (|x|^p + |y|^p)^{1/p}$ is the $\ell^p$ norm.
nodes.title: The squared $\ell^p$ norm of $(1, 1)$ for finite $p$

nodes.summary: For every extended real $p \in [1, \infty]$, in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^p$ norm the vectors $u = (1, 1)$ and $v = (1, -1)$ satisfy $\|u - v\| = 2$.
nodes.title: The difference of the parallelogram witnesses has norm two

nodes.summary: Let $p \in [1, \infty]$ with $p \neq 2$. Then the normed space $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^p$ norm carries no real inner product space structure, that is, there is no real inner product with $\langle x, x \rangle = \|x\|^2$ for every $x$.
nodes.title: The $\ell^p$ norm on $\mathbb{R}^2$ comes from no inner product unless $p = 2$

nodes.summary: In $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^1$ norm there exist vectors $x \neq y$ with $\|x\| = \|y\| = 1$ and $\|\tfrac{1}{2} (x + y)\| = 1$.
nodes.title: Two distinct $\ell^1$ unit vectors in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with a unit midpoint

nodes.summary: In $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^\infty$ norm there exist vectors $x \neq y$ with $\|x\| = \|y\| = 1$ and $\|\tfrac{1}{2} (x + y)\| = 1$.
nodes.title: Two distinct $\ell^\infty$ unit vectors in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with a unit midpoint

nodes.summary: The real normed space $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^1$ norm is not a strictly convex space: not every closed ball of positive radius centred at the origin is a strictly convex set.
nodes.title: $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^1$ norm is not strictly convex

nodes.summary: The real normed space $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^\infty$ norm is not a strictly convex space: not every closed ball of positive radius centred at the origin is a strictly convex set.
nodes.title: $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^\infty$ norm is not strictly convex

nodes.summary: Let $p \in [1, \infty]$ and equip $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^p$ norm. The vectors $u = (1, 1)$ and $v = (1, -1)$ satisfy $\|u + v\|^2 + \|u - v\|^2 = 2 (\|u\|^2 + \|v\|^2)$ if and only if $p = 2$.
nodes.title: The parallelogram law for $(1, 1)$ and $(1, -1)$ holds only for the $\ell^2$ norm

nodes.summary: Let $p \in [1, \infty]$ with $p \neq 2$ and equip $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^p$ norm. Then the vectors $u = (1, 1)$ and $v = (1, -1)$ satisfy $\|u + v\|^2 + \|u - v\|^2 \neq 2 (\|u\|^2 + \|v\|^2)$.
nodes.title: The parallelogram law fails on $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^p$ norm for $p \neq 2$

nodes.summary: Let $1 < p < \infty$ and equip $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^p$ norm. If $x \neq y$ are vectors with $\|x\| = \|y\| = 1$, then $\|\tfrac{1}{2} (x + y)\| < 1$.
nodes.title: Midpoints of distinct $\ell^p$ unit vectors in $\mathbb{R}^2$ have norm less than one

nodes.summary: For $1 < p < \infty$, the real normed space $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^p$ norm is a strictly convex space: every closed ball of positive radius centred at the origin is a strictly convex set.
nodes.title: $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the $\ell^p$ norm is strictly convex for $1 < p < \infty$

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
